content:
In sooth mine own dear friend who dost crave to tread the fair and fabled lands of Nippon let this humble scribe weave for thee a journey most wondrous and full of marvels both ancient and new.

**Day the First**

Upon the morn whenas the sun doth rise and paint the heavens with hues of gold and crimson thou shalt set foot in the mighty city of Tokyoe. First repair unto the sacred grounds of the Meiji Shrine where the spirits of emperors past do dwell in quiet repose. Then wander forth to the bustling thoroughfares of Harajuku where the youth of the land do don their most fanciful attire and partake in sweets most sugared and bright.

At noon take thy ease in the gardens of the Imperial Palace where the stones do whisper tales of old and the waters do reflect the sky so blue. When the day doth wane repair unto the district of Shinjuku where the lights do twinkle like stars fallen to earth and the izakayas do offer repast most bounteous.

**Day the Second**

With the break of day embark upon a journey by swift train unto the ancient capital of Kyoto a city steeped in tradition and grace. First visit the hallowed halls of Kinkaku-ji the Golden Pavilion where the roof doth gleam like burnished gold and the gardens do sing with the voices of nature.

At noon feast upon the delicacies of the land in the Gion quarter where the geishas do glide like ghosts of beauty past. Then wander unto the Fushimi Inari Shrine where a thousand torii gates do form a path unto the heavens and the air is thick with incense and prayer.

When the moon doth rise take thy rest in a ryokan most humble where the tatami mats do cradle thy bones and the onsen doth cleanse thy spirit of the dust of travel.

**Day the Third**

Arise with the lark and make thy way unto the bamboo groves of Arashiyama where the stalks do whisper secrets in the wind and the river doth flow with purpose yet serene. Then venture forth unto the temples of the Philosopher’s Path where the stones do bear the footprints of sages long gone.

At noon dine upon the delights of the Nishiki Market where the vendors do cry their wares with voices most merry and the seafood doth gleam like pearls plucked from the deep.

In the afternoon take thy leave of Kyoto and return unto the bustling embrace of Tokyoe. Spend the eve in the district of Asakusa where the Senso-ji Temple doth stand as a beacon of faith and the lanterns do glow like fireflies trapped in amber.

**Day the Fourth**

When the dawn doth break once more take thou a train unto the sacred isle of Miyajima where the torii gate of Itsukushima doth float upon the waters like a dream most fleeting. Walk the paths of the island where the deer do roam as lords of the land and the momiji manju do tempt thee with their sweet embrace.

At noon partake in the feast of the oysters most plump and the sake most crisp and cold. Then climb the mountain unto the summit where the views do stretch unto the sea and the heavens do kiss the earth.

When the sun doth set return unto the mainland and make thy way back unto Tokyoe. Spend thy final eve in the district of Roppongi where the lights do dance and the music doth fill the air with revelry most grand.

**Day the Fifth**

Upon the morn whenas the last of thy time in this fair land doth wane take thou a final stroll through the gardens of Ueno where the cherry blossoms do fall like snow upon the earth. Then repair unto the markets where the last of thy souvenirs thou mayst procure before taking thy leave.

When the hour of the wolf doth come make thou thy way unto the airport where the planes do stand like great birds of metal ready to bear thee home. Yet fear not for the memories thou hast made in this land of the rising sun shall dwell in thy heart for all time to come.

Fare thee well good traveler and may thy journey be filled with wonder and delight.
